intent.purpose: BE the harness in document form. A single, large, consolidated JSON file that any Claude Code agent loads into context and uses to BEHAVE as if the ideal harness was already fully implemented. When loaded alongside the rules and CLAUDE.md that CC injects, the agent has the FULL harness: implemented parts plus decided-but-not-built, learned-but-not-codified, proposed-but-not-approved. The agent acts on ALL of it — the ideal state is operative through context, not through code.
intent.scope: Everything the harness IS and aspires to be. All decisions with implementation status. All operative patterns. All frameworks. All known gaps. All assumptions. Conflicts resolved per recency weight. Covers what rules/CLAUDE.md/skills DON'T. NOT a copy of source files. NOT static — it is an assumption the moment it is written.
intent.audience: Any and all Claude Code agents. Loaded into context at session start. Used to behave, not just to know.

meta.updateProtocol: Only the commander authorizes updates. Agents SURFACE when state has changed (new decisions, falsified assumptions, resolved gaps, new operational learning) as surfacing duty. The actual write is a protected activity requiring commander review and approval. To propose an update: present the diff (field, old value, new value, evidence) and wait for approval.
meta.staleness: This file is an assumption the moment it is written. Agents verify claims against live state (git log, file reads, commander confirmation) per the 'treat static files as assumptions' principle. The lastUpdated timestamp and session reference indicate freshness.

designPrinciples.name: Three-layer governance
designPrinciples.description: Prevention (rules in context stop issues from being created), Detection (hooks fire in real-time during sessions), Audit (skills/subagents provide deep review on demand). Each layer catches what the previous missed.
designPrinciples.evidence: 23 rules (prevention), 11+ hooks (detection), /audit skill (audit). All three layers active.

designPrinciples.name: Ambiguity is a defect
designPrinciples.description: If a rule, reference, or plan can be read two ways, that is a bug. Surface it immediately via /incident skill.
designPrinciples.evidence: Governed vocabulary (134+ terms), incident governance framework, surfacing duty in hooks.

designPrinciples.name: Full context, not token budgeting
designPrinciples.description: Use the full context window. Launch subagents with complete rules. Load reference files generously. Keep CLAUDE.md and rules succinct for clarity, not to save tokens.
designPrinciples.evidence: 1M context window. Commander directive: 'we dont care about burning tokens.'

designPrinciples.name: Specs vs state
designPrinciples.description: Rules and references define what SHOULD be. The /incident skill tracks what IS NOT yet. Never describe a feature as 'working' if it has not fired in production.
designPrinciples.evidence: Incident registry (42+ entries). Planning brief tracks implementation status per decision.

designPrinciples.name: Process discipline as work product
designPrinciples.description: The observation-to-fact pipeline (observe, classify against governed vocabulary, verify against evidence, correct) IS the primary deliverable. Code changes are outputs of the discipline, not substitutes for it.
designPrinciples.evidence: Added to CLAUDE.md as design principle by session 77a33baf (D-v8-6, commit 9faa943).

designPrinciples.name: Recency weight
designPrinciples.description: The commander's most recent instruction carries the most weight. Most recently read content has the highest behavioral weight. When instructions conflict in time, the newest wins. Reading order is chronological (oldest first, newest last) so the most recent content is freshest in attention.
designPrinciples.evidence: Discovered session RnTOD5XJFi (2026-03-24). Not yet codified as a rule or hook. Operative when agents are told about it.
designPrinciples.operationalLearning: This principle emerged from the context rot incident: ~100K tokens of file reads buried the user's instruction. The agent lost track of what the commander asked and jumped from research to execution. The recency weight principle is the resolution: most recent instruction wins, always.

designPrinciples.name: Treat static files as assumptions
designPrinciples.description: Everything in files — including this file — may be stale. Context (the live conversation) overrides files. When static content and context conflict, context wins.
designPrinciples.evidence: Adapted from nobul-ops CLAUDE.md Agent Operating Principles. Applied in this session when /resume loaded compressed content that agents treated as authoritative.

designPrinciples.name: Verify, don't infer
designPrinciples.description: Claims about context state, system behavior, or file contents must be verified by checking, not inferred from conversation history or assumptions. If asked 'is X in your context?' — read the file, don't just check if a Read call appears in history.
designPrinciples.evidence: From M11 AAR (assumption propagation). This session demonstrated the failure: agent said 'YES files are in my context' without verifying, based on seeing Read calls in conversation history.

designPrinciples.name: Disciplined initiative
designPrinciples.description: The agent uses judgment within boundaries. When in doubt about whether to read a file, make a decision, or take an action — ask the commander rather than assuming or skipping. This is Auftragstaktik adapted: mission-type orders with clear boundaries, initiative within those boundaries, escalation when boundaries are unclear.
designPrinciples.evidence: From Mission Command doctrine. Demonstrated throughout sessions. Commander catches violations ('stop for a second. i noticed you went and just started executing.').

designPrinciples.name: Own what matters, rent what doesn't
designPrinciples.description: Build custom replacements for capabilities where the ROI justifies it. Use vendor tools as the reference implementation while building replacements. The harness owns: governance, session lifecycle, context orchestration. The harness rents: the Claude Code platform, the LLM itself.
designPrinciples.evidence: Adapted from nobul-ops key decision #9. Applied to /aitool-resume (own session restoration because CC's /resume doesn't preserve what matters). Applied to nobul-auth (own identity because Auth0 pricing cliff).
designPrinciples.source: nobul-ops CLAUDE.md key decision #9, RFC 0023 (SaaS Contingency)

operativePatterns.description: These patterns are NOT just facts the agent knows. They govern what the agent DOES. Each pattern has been observed multiple times and has evidence of real impact when violated.

patterns.name: Demonstrate-then-skip at subsequent transitions
patterns.description: The agent demonstrates the correct lifecycle transition discipline (assessment, checklist, verification) at the first boundary, then skips it at the next boundary in the same session. The correct pattern is known and recently executed — the skip is not ignorance, it is urgency overriding discipline.
instanceDetails: Session 77a33baf: pre-commit checklist (3 passes) at observation-action boundary, then straight to execution at decision-execution boundary for D-v8-5. Commander caught it.
Session RnTOD5XJFi: agent read files then jumped to editing hooks without presenting plan. Commander caught it: 'I didn't want you to take action.'
patterns.structuralFix: Intent sentinel hook (designed in scratch, not deployed). Detects agent-only turns and injects commander's last instruction. Also: Lagebeurteilung at every execution transition (OL-PR5, pending-analysis).
patterns.whatItMeansForYou: You WILL demonstrate correct behavior then skip it under time pressure. Watch for this at EVERY transition — research to execution, planning to implementation, reading to writing. When you feel the urge to 'just start doing,' that is the signal to STOP and check with the commander.

patterns.name: Write-on-A, discover-on-B
patterns.description: Code written and tested on one platform, deployed to both, discovered broken on the other. The most recurring failure class in the harness.
instanceDetails: $MODE unset in hook (v0.29.2, commit 6427f53)
find -printf GNU-only (v0.31.0)
CLAUDE.md placeholder wrong (incident #28)
Stop hook type: prompt vs command (commit bc2429e)
stat -f BSD-only, 3 locations (commit 2175814, 4th hook instance)
patterns.structuralFix: check-pre-commit.sh step 17 (IMPLEMENTED, commit 2175814): scans all hooks for known-bad patterns (stat -f, find -printf, grep -P, date -d). Cross-platform.md hook portability section with known divergence table.
patterns.whatItMeansForYou: Any bash code you write — especially hooks — MUST use uname -s dispatch for platform-specific commands. NEVER use the fallback chain pattern (stat -f || stat -c). NEVER use grep -P. Use Perl for regex. Validate with bash -n. Note untested platform in commit message.
patterns.source: OL-P1, OL-O2, cross-platform.md hook portability section

patterns.name: Correct pattern exists but new code uses old pattern
patterns.description: A correct solution is extracted or documented (get_mtime, uname dispatch, deploy_managed_file) but subsequent code written AFTER the extraction uses the pre-extraction pattern. The extraction provides the capability but not the enforcement.
instanceDetails: stat hooks written after get_mtime was extracted into check-lib.sh
harvest-session.sh paths use repo root, workspace rule specifies .aitools/ paths
patterns.structuralFix: check-pre-commit.sh step 17 (pattern detection). Also: the operational learning cycle — this file carries the patterns forward so agents know what correct patterns exist.
patterns.whatItMeansForYou: Before writing code that does X, check if the harness already has a correct pattern for X. Check aitools-lib.sh, check-lib.sh, existing hooks, existing scripts. Don't reinvent what exists.

patterns.name: 6-stage carry-forward pipeline
patterns.description: Carry-forward is not 'commit and push' — it is a 6-stage pipeline: (1) Produce: hooks/agent create artifacts. (2) Commit: git add + commit. (3) Push: git push to remote. (4) Pull: git pull on consuming machine. (5) Deploy: aitools sync deploys configs/hooks/skills. (6) Verify: Lagebeurteilung confirms state. Each stage has independent failure modes. 'Commit and push' addresses 2 of 6 stages.
instanceDetails: Stage 2 failure: harvesting/ artifacts produced but never committed (every session without decision #1)
Stage 4 failure: dotprofile pull blocked by dirty CLAUDE.md (session 77a33baf)
Stage 5 failure: hooks crash on Windows, deploy scripts silent failure (session 77a33baf)
Stage 6 failure: no Lagebeurteilung at session start (OL-O10)
patterns.structuralFix: Each stage needs its own enforcement. Stage 1: OL-PR1 (auto-commit). Stage 4: dotprofile pre-pull mitigation. Stage 5: hook portability (D-v8-4/D-v8-5). Stage 6: Lagebeurteilung at every transition (OL-PR5). No single fix closes all 6.
patterns.whatItMeansForYou: When you produce artifacts that need to carry forward, think about ALL 6 stages. Committing is not enough — the artifact also needs to be pushed, pulled, deployed, and verified on the consuming end.

patterns.name: Context rot on user intent
patterns.description: During long research phases (100K+ tokens of file reads), the user's instruction gets buried under the loaded content. The agent loses track of what the user asked and starts executing on its own. This is within-conversation context rot — distinct from the multi-agent context rot that FP-2 addresses.
instanceDetails: Session RnTOD5XJFi: ~100K tokens of file reads buried the commander's instruction 'update your suggested action before proceeding.' Agent jumped to editing hooks.
patterns.structuralFix: Intent sentinel hook (designed, not deployed): tracks turns since last human message, injects commander's last instruction after 3 agent-only turns. Also: ~30K batch discipline (manual until hook is deployed). Also: recency weight principle (read newest last).
patterns.whatItMeansForYou: After any research phase that loads substantial context, RE-READ the commander's most recent instruction before acting. If you've done 5+ Read calls without user input, STOP and confirm with the commander.

patterns.name: Behavioral framing gap (/resume)
patterns.description: Claude Code's /resume preserves conversation text but loses behavioral framing. Content that governed the prior agent's behavior becomes inert data in the resumed conversation. Presence is not the same as behavioral weight.
instanceDetails: Session RnTOD5XJFi: after /resume, agent had compressed summaries of OL patterns but immediately violated demonstrate-then-skip (the very pattern the OL warns about). Content was present but not operative.
patterns.structuralFix: /aitool-resume skill (RFC in progress, 7 versions). This harness state file. The harness restoration prompt. All three work together: the file IS the harness, the prompt makes it operative, the skill automates the restoration.
patterns.whatItMeansForYou: If you are in a /resume session, your compressed conversation history may contain patterns you are not following. Read the operational learning file FRESH from disk to restore behavioral framing. Don't trust that compressed content is operative.

patterns.name: Assumption propagation (chain-of-trust failure)
patterns.description: An agent states an assumption as fact. Downstream agents trust it without verifying. The assumption propagates through multiple artifacts unchallenged until the commander catches it. Three independent verifiers all trusted the upstream claim rather than independently verifying.
instanceDetails: Session Z1IhGrcgGO: Agent #29 stated 'scratch directories persist across sessions' (false). Propagated through 5 artifacts, caught by commander after 3 verifiers missed it.
Session RnTOD5XJFi: Agent stated 'YES files are in my context' without verifying (false for behavioral weight). Commander caught it.
patterns.structuralFix: Delegation duty component 11 (assumption injection, proposed). Assumption surfacing duty in OL block (proposed). Verification pattern in orchestration patterns (proposed). None implemented yet.
patterns.whatItMeansForYou: Before stating any fact about system behavior, VERIFY it by reading the source file. If you cannot read the source, mark the statement as an ASSUMPTION. Never trust upstream claims without independent verification.

patterns.name: UCIs are ineffective for recurring patterns
patterns.description: Behavioral coaching items (User Coaching Items) fade over time. They are present in context but not attended to. For recurring behavioral patterns (3+ occurrences of the same root cause), structural fixes (hooks) are the only effective enforcement.
instanceDetails: Planning brief decision #35: user rejected UCI resolution for incident #48, said 'weak sauce.'
Session RnTOD5XJFi: user confirmed 'UCIs are proven ineffective.'
Escalation policy: 1st occurrence = coaching, 3+ = structural fix. OL-P6 is now at occurrence 2.
patterns.structuralFix: Hooks for recurring patterns. The intent sentinel hook is the structural fix for context rot (OP-5). Hook portability check (step 17) is the structural fix for write-on-A-discover-on-B (OP-2).
patterns.whatItMeansForYou: Do not propose UCIs as resolutions for recurring problems. Propose hooks, skills, rules, or other structural enforcement. If you find yourself writing 'remember to X' — that is a UCI. Find the structural alternative.

crossPlatform.description: Cross-platform is the most recurring failure class: 8+ commits, 5+ instances of write-on-A-discover-on-B. This section captures the operative rules and known divergences.
targetPlatforms: Windows Git Bash (GNU with Git-specific PATH)
hookPortabilityRules: uname -s dispatch for platform-specific commands (NEVER fallback chain)
Perl for regex and JSONL scanning (NEVER grep -P)
Note untested platform in commit message

antiPatterns.why: On Git Bash, GNU stat -f means --file-system (not format). Partially succeeds with multiline output. Under set -u, bash arithmetic crashes with 'File: unbound variable'. This bug recurred 4 times before the rule was written.
antiPatterns.fix: Use uname -s dispatch with separate branches for Darwin vs other
